summary: Phase 149O.1F -- HATP Repository Identity + Trust-Store Foundation Independent Verification: independently attacked the Wave 1/2 foundation implemented by 149O.1E rather than trusting its report. Reconstructed the production diff (repository_identity.py, hatp_bootstrap.py, commands/init.py, templates.py, .pcae/.gitignore -- all classified, zero unrelated hunks), the requirement mapping from HATP-001, the repository-identity model, and the trust-store model directly from source. Independently reproduced sound: caller-controlled-ID rejection at every production API surface; malformed-identity fail-closed with no auto-heal; symlink write refusal both before and after atomic write; zero static/hardcoded identity in templates.py (whose only diff is one .gitignore line); clone non-propagation (identity path gitignored, confirmed via `git check-ignore -v`); full-copy and repository-ID-theft attacks resolving to no authorized deployment; worktree-distinct identity; path-move identity preservation with no auto-rebind; same-ID-wrong-root and same-root-wrong-ID both rejected; canonical-root `.`/`..`/symlink aliasing resolving identically; strict closed-schema registry validation with duplicate principal/signer/binding/authority records rejected outright (grep-confirmed absence of any mtime/file-order-based selection logic); no wildcard/global authority fallback; this repository's live deployment and every agent-controllable permission mode never reporting READY; a monkeypatched root-UID probe still routing through the same-user check; zero public mutation methods on HATPTrustStore; zero approval_present/HATP_TRUSTED_OPERATIONAL/verify_* symbols in either module; RAE/Permission-Broker/agent modules byte-identical since the 149O.1B.3 freeze; and the `repository_identity` string's unrelated pre-existing use as a plain field name elsewhere in cltr/cltr_prototype confirmed to import nothing from this phase's module. Found one BLOCKING defect: HATPTrustStore.production() -> _default_production_trust_root() -> Path.home() consults the ordinary, agent-controllable $HOME process-environment variable (verified directly: setting HOME relocates Path.home()), letting an agent redirect the 'authoritative' trust-store root to a self-owned directory and obtain a real, non-None DeploymentBinding match from a self-authored registry.json -- contradicting the module's own claimed environment-independence invariant and the 149O.1E adversarial suite, which checked four guessed HATP-specific variable names but never HOME, the actual resolver dependency. resolve_deployment_authorization does not compose with the (independently sound) same-user environment_status() check, so nothing in Wave-1/2 itself prevents a future consumer from trusting a HOME-redirected binding. Per the independent-verification charter, this defect was recorded and reproduced but not repaired; no production source was modified (git diff --name-only HEAD -- src/pcae/ is empty). Verdict: NOT VERIFIED -- BLOCKING HATP FOUNDATION FINDING. Foundation software NOT READY pending a narrow trust-store path hardening repair; HATP production remains NOT READY regardless (Waves 3-7 unimplemented). B-149O-1..4 remain OPEN, reproduced identically via the full Permission-Broker/RAE regression run. New independent adversarial suite (tests/test_phase_149o_1f_hatp_repository_identity_trust_store_foundation_independent_verification.py): 22/22 passing.
